brief: Goldman's weekly prime and sales-trading rundown: the S&P 500 rose 1.2% on the week (Nasdaq 100 +3.25%, Russell 2000 -0.68%) as investors digested a sharp rate ramp, an evolving AI trade, and strong sentiment surveys. Meta's Muse app launch drove over 900,000 downloads in six days and an 11% Monday pop in META shares, reviving the momentum trade (High Beta Momentum basket, nine-day win streak) while the Consumer Inertia basket underperformed. Hedge funds net sold Healthcare for a sixth straight week, with selling magnitude in the 98th percentile, rotating into Info Tech, the top dollar-bought sector for a fourth week; institutional and CTA futures length was trimmed (index futures net length fell from 48% in May to 36%, CTA global equity length from about $145bn to $70bn), which Goldman says makes the technical setup less unfavorable, though a $32bn pension rebalancing sale looms into month end. Hot flash PMIs plus an oil surge pushed the 30-year yield to its highest since 2004 Thursday before easing Friday as oil retreated; Goldman argues this makes shorting its Non-Profitable Tech basket compelling. Iran's conditional Hormuz-reopening proposal and an extended US-China trade truce offered late-week relief.
